summary: Shared-memory broadcast no longer drops a write notification
details: The writer's notify socket had a send high-water mark of 1, so a notification sent within about 1 ms (x86) or 3 ms (aarch64) of the previous one was dropped. A reader that had parked in between then slept until its 5 s recheck. With a short VLLM_SHM_BROADCAST_BUSY_LOOP_S this stalled requests for seconds; on 4x GB10 about a third of warm resends took 1.2-10.8 s instead of 0.1-0.4 s.
The socket now keeps the default high-water mark; the readers' conflating queue already collapses a burst of notifications into one.
